mainTopic: מנשה's תשובה, aggadot about the last kings of יהודה, and רב חסדא's teachings on משלי and תהלים 91
overview: The amud opens with the end of a view that מנשה never did תשובה. רבי יוחנן rejects it: saying מנשה has no share in עולם הבא discourages people who repent. A ברייתא uses the years of his reign to show he repented for thirty-three years. The odd word 'ויחתר' teaches that הקב״ה dug a kind of tunnel in heaven to accept him, getting around מדת הדין. Next, רבי שמעון בן יוחי explains why 'בראשית' is used for יהויקים and צדקיהו: the world nearly went back to תוהו ובוהו in their days and was saved. He also shows that wicked kings like אחז and אמציה turned to idols whether הקב״ה punished them or was kind to them. He then explains that the princes of בבל sat in the very place where הלכות were decided. After a סימן, רב חסדא gives three teachings: the neglected field as five kings who ruined the kingdom, the four groups who do not greet the שכינה, and the blessings of תהלים 91, which are split into the father's, the mother's, and finally Heaven's. That last blessing continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of an explanation: because מנשה did not repent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier explanation of the words 'בגלל מנשה': the reason given is that מנשה did not do תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Because of מנשה' means: because he did not repent.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of an earlier discussion. The גמרא is explaining that the פסוק's words 'because of מנשה' mean 'because מנשה did not do תשובה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line belongs to a view that holds מנשה never repented. It is the view רבי יוחנן is about to reject strongly in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final opinion about מנשה. It is the tail end of one view, and רבי יוחנן argues against it right away.

phrases.english: "Because of Menashe"
phrases.notes: From ירמיהו 15:4, the פסוק the גמרא was just talking about.

phrases.english: means: because he did not repent.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּגְלַל מְנַשֶּׁה, דְּלָא עֲבַד תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation that began before this section.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'because of מנשה' refer to the fact that he did not repent.

steps.title: Saying מנשה has no share discourages people who repent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says anyone who claims מנשה has no share in עולם הבא weakens the hands of people doing תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Anyone who says מנשה has no share in the World to Come weakens the hands of those who repent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a strong statement. You should not say מנשה lost his share in עולם הבא, because that discourages people who want to do תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone as wicked as מנשה repented and still lost everything, a sinner might think: why bother? רבי יוחנן holds that מנשה really did do תשובה, and that teaching otherwise sends a harmful message.

keyTerms.meaning: a share in the World to Come
weakens their hands, makes them lose heart

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that how we teach about past sinners affects real people trying to change today.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who says that Menashe
has no share in the World to Come
weakens the hands of those who repent.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר מְנַשֶּׁה אֵין לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the view in step 1 that מנשה did not repent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must not say מנשה has no share in עולם הבא, because he did תשובה, and saying otherwise discourages penitents.

steps.title: A ברייתא: מנשה repented for thirty-three years
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited before רבי יוחנן that מנשה repented for 33 years, and pointed to the פסוקים about his reign and his sins like אחאב.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a תנא taught before רבי יוחנן: מנשה repented for thirty-three years, as it says: 'מנשה was twelve when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem… and he made an אשרה… as אחאב king of Israel had done.'
steps.whatsHappening: Support for רבי יוחנן is brought from a ברייתא. It says מנשה repented for 33 years and quotes the פסוקים that will be used to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on two numbers: מנשה ruled 55 years, and he sinned 'like אחאב.' The math comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: a scholar who memorized and recited ברייתות
a tree or pole used for idol worship
a wicked king of the northern kingdom of Israel

phrases.english: For a tanna taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
Menashe repented
for thirty-three years,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the square-bracket wording just drops the extra ל. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"Menashe was twelve years old when he became king,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 21:1-3

phrases.english: and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem
and he made an asherah, etc.,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'did evil' (round brackets). The corrected wording reads 'made an אשרה,' the part of the פסוק that compares him to אחאב.

phrases.english: as Achav king of Israel had done."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up רבי יוחנן's claim that מנשה repented.

steps.title: The math: 55 minus 22 equals 33
steps.stepSummary: אחאב ruled 22 years and מנשה ruled 55. Subtracting the 22 years of sinning like אחאב leaves 33 years of תשובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How long did אחאב reign? Twenty-two years. How long did מנשה reign? Fifty-five. Take away twenty-two, and thirty-three remain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא does the arithmetic. 'Like אחאב' is read as 'for as many years as אחאב reigned,' which is 22, and the rest of מנשה's 55 years were years of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to אחאב is read as a measure of time, not just a description of the sin. 22 years of sin out of 55 leaves 33 years, which the ברייתא counts as years of repentance.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא, מנשה did תשובה for 33 years, so we must not say he lost his share in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: How many years did Achav reign?
Twenty-two years.
How many years did Menashe reign?
Fifty-five.
Subtract from them twenty-two,
phrases.notes: These are the years מנשה sinned 'like אחאב,' one for each year אחאב was king.

phrases.english: and thirty-three remain.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּמָּה מָלַךְ אַחְאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof by doing the calculation from the פסוקים quoted in step 3.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Comparing the length of אחאב's and מנשה's reigns

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say 'ויחתר' instead of 'ויעתר'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, asks about the unusual word 'ויחתר' in the פסוק about מנשה's prayer. The normal word would be 'ויעתר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What does the פסוק mean, 'He listened to him and ויחתר to him'? It should have said 'ויעתר לו,' He accepted his plea!
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching about מנשה's תשובה begins. The גמרא points out a strange spelling in the פסוק and asks why it is there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ויעתר' with an ע means 'He accepted the prayer.' 'ויחתר' with a ח sounds like 'digging.' The question sets up a lesson about how מנשה's תשובה was accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the meaning of what is written

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"And He listened to him, and vayechater to him"?
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 33:13

phrases.english: It should have said "vaye'ater lo," He accepted his plea!
phrases.notes: The two words differ by one letter, ח or ע. The ח version sounds like 'dig.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וַיִּשְׁמַע אֵלָיו וַיֵּחָתֶר לוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching that shows מנשה's תשובה was accepted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses 'ויחתר' instead of the expected 'ויעתר'

steps.title: הקב״ה dug a tunnel in heaven to accept מנשה
steps.stepSummary: The odd word teaches that הקב״ה made a kind of tunnel in heaven to accept מנשה's תשובה, getting around מדת הדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that הקב״ה made a kind of tunnel in heaven for him, in order to accept him in repentance, because of the attribute of strict justice.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers the question. 'ויחתר' comes from 'מחתרת,' a tunnel: הקב״ה opened a hidden way in heaven so מנשה's תשובה could come through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strict justice would have blocked someone as wicked as מנשה. So הקב״ה accepted him through a 'tunnel' that went around the normal gate. This backs up רבי יוחנן's point that even מנשה's תשובה was accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: a tunnel, a hole dug through

steps.whatToRemember: מנשה's תשובה was accepted. The 'tunnel' teaches that הקב״ה makes a way for a sincere penitent even when strict justice would say no.

phrases.aramaic: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, made for him
a kind of tunnel in heaven,
in order to accept him in repentance,
because of the attribute of strict justice.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָשָׂה לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כְּמִין מַחְתֶּרֶת בָּרָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ויחתר' hints at a tunnel הקב״ה dug in heaven to accept מנשה's תשובה despite מדת הדין.

steps.title: Why 'at the beginning of the reign' only for יהויקים and צדקיהו?
steps.stepSummary: A new teaching from רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי asks why the פסוקים use 'בראשית ממלכת' for יהויקים and צדקיהו, as if there had been no kings before them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What is meant by 'At the beginning of the reign of יהויקים son of יאשיהו,' and 'At the beginning of the reign of צדקיהו'? Were there no kings until now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new question: why are these two kings described with the special word 'בראשית'? Steps 8 and 9 answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בראשית' sounds like the very first beginning, as if kingship started with these kings. Since many kings came before them, the word seems out of place, and the גמרא will explain what it hints at.

keyTerms.meaning: at the beginning of the reign
a late king of יהודה, son of יאשיהו

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"At the beginning of the reign of Yehoyakim son of Yoshiyahu,"
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 26:1

phrases.english: and it is written: "At the beginning of the reign of Tzidkiyahu"?
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 28:1

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עַד הָאִידָּנָא לָא הֲווֹ מַלְכֵי?
phrases.english: But until now, were there no kings?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״בְּרֵאשִׁית מַמְלֶכֶת יְהוֹיָקִים בֶּן יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching from the same pair of rabbis, now about a different פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוקים use 'בראשית' for these two kings when many kings came before them

steps.title: The world was almost destroyed because of יהויקים
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה wanted to return the world to תוהו ובוהו because of יהויקים. He looked at יהויקים's generation and calmed down.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, הקב״ה wanted to turn the whole world back into chaos because of יהויקים. Then He looked at יהויקים's generation, and His mind was calmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7 about why the פסוק calls יהויקים's reign a 'beginning.' The world nearly ended in his time, so its survival was like a fresh start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'בראשית' hints at the creation of the world. Because the world was almost sent back to before creation and then saved, his reign is described as a new 'beginning.' The good people still alive in his generation are what calmed הקב״ה's anger.

keyTerms.meaning: Chaos and emptiness, the state of the world before creation
His mind cooled down, He was calmed
his generation (here, the generation of יהויקים)

steps.confusionAlert: It was not יהויקים who saved the world. He was the cause of the anger. It was the people of his generation who calmed הקב״ה.

phrases.english: Rather, the Holy One, Blessed be He, sought
to return the entire world
to chaos and void on account of Yehoyakim.
phrases.notes: These are the words from בראשית 1:2 describing the world before creation, which is why 'בראשית' fits.

phrases.english: He looked at his generation,
and His mind was calmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בִּקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחְזִיר אֶת הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לְתוֹהוּ וָבוֹהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק says 'בראשית ממלכת' for יהויקים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The world almost returned to תוהו ובוהו in his time and was saved, so it was like a new beginning

steps.title: The world was almost destroyed because of צדקיהו's generation
steps.stepSummary: Here it is the reverse. הקב״ה wanted to destroy the world because of צדקיהו's generation, and He was calmed by looking at צדקיהו himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה wanted to turn the whole world back into chaos because of צדקיהו's generation. Then He looked at צדקיהו, and His mind was calmed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same kind of answer for צדקיהו, the second king called 'בראשית ממלכת.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is flipped. With יהויקים, the king was bad and the generation saved the world. With צדקיהו, the generation was bad and the king saved the world.

keyTerms.meaning: צדקיהו, the last king of יהודה before the חורבן

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, sought
to return the entire world

phrases.aramaic: לְתוֹהוּ וָבוֹהוּ בִּשְׁבִיל דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל צִדְקִיָּה.
phrases.english: to chaos and void on account of the generation of Tzidkiyahu.
He looked at Tzidkiyahu
and His mind was calmed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּקֵּשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְהַחְזִיר אֶת הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לְתוֹהוּ וָבוֹהוּ בִּשְׁבִיל דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל צִדְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel answer for the second king mentioned in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק says 'בראשית ממלכת' for צדקיהו
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The world was saved in the merit of צדקיהו himself, so it was like a new beginning

steps.title: But the פסוק says צדקיהו did evil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that צדקיהו was good, because the פסוק says he did evil in הקב״ה's eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about צדקיהו it is also written: 'And he did evil in the eyes of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the previous step. How could צדקיהו be the merit that saved the world if a פסוק calls him evil?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 treats צדקיהו as righteous enough to calm הקב״ה. The פסוק in מלכים seems to say the opposite, so the two appear to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he did evil in the eyes of ה׳'

phrases.english: About Tzidkiyahu too it is written:
"And he did evil in the eyes of the Lord."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 24:19

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּצִדְקִיָּה נָמֵי כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim in step 9 that צדקיהו was worthy
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that הקב״ה was calmed by looking at צדקיהו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says צדקיהו did evil, so he could not be a merit for the world

steps.title: His 'evil' was not protesting
steps.stepSummary: צדקיהו could have protested against his generation's sins and did not. That failure is what the פסוק calls 'evil.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It was in his power to protest, and he did not protest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. צדקיהו was personally good, but he is blamed for not stopping the people around him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'evil' in the פסוק does not describe his own actions. It refers to his failure to use his power to stop others. So he can be righteous himself and still be held responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: To protest, to stop others from sinning
In his power, literally 'in his hand'

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a strong idea: someone who has the power to stop wrongdoing and stays silent is held responsible, as if he did it himself.

phrases.english: For it was in his power to protest
and he did not protest.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה בְּיָדוֹ לִמְחוֹת וְלֹא מִיחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means צדקיהו himself was wicked
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means he failed to protest against others, but he himself was righteous

steps.title: What does the פסוק about the wise man and the fool mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, asks what the פסוק in משלי means: whether the wise man is angry or laughs, the fool gives him no rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: What does the פסוק mean, 'A wise man who argues with a foolish man, whether he is angry or laughs, there is no rest'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching from the same pair of חכמים. It asks for the meaning of a פסוק in משלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question sets up a reading where the 'wise man' is הקב״ה and the 'fool' is the sinning king. The next steps show both 'anger' and 'laughing.'

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written
He is angry, or he laughs/smiles
There is no rest, no calm

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
What is that which is written:
"A wise man who contends with a foolish man,
phrases.notes: משלי 29:9

phrases.english: whether he is angry or laughs, there is no rest"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same חכמים quoted in steps 5 and 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the פסוק in משלי about the wise man and the fool

steps.title: Anger at אחז led him to idols
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה was angry at אחז and let the kings of Damascus beat him. אחז responded by sacrificing to their gods.
steps.simpleTranslation: הקב״ה said: I was angry at אחז and handed him over to the kings of Damascus. He sacrificed and burned incense to their gods, as the פסוק says: 'He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus who struck him, and said, because the gods of the kings of ארם help them, I will sacrifice to them and they will help me. But they made him and all of ישראל stumble.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the פסוק. This is the 'angry' half: punishment did not bring אחז back, and it pushed him toward idols.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment was meant to make אחז do תשובה. He drew the wrong conclusion and decided the winners' gods must be powerful. This is the 'fool' who gives the wise man no rest even when he is angry.

keyTerms.meaning: אחז, a wicked king of יהודה
To make him stumble, to ruin him

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
I was angry at Achaz
and I gave him into the hand of the kings of Damascus;
he sacrificed and burned incense [to their gods],
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; the corrected wording adds them.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"He sacrificed to the gods of Darmesek who struck him,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 28:23. 'דרמשק' is another spelling of Damascus.

phrases.english: and he said: [Because] the gods of the kings of Aram,
they help them,
to them I will sacrifice and they will help me;
but they were [for him] the cause of his stumbling
and of all Israel."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: כָּעַסְתִּי עַל אָחָז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'angry' (רגז) part of the פסוק from step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When הקב״ה was angry at אחז, אחז turned to the gods of his enemies

steps.title: Kindness to אמציה also led him to idols
steps.stepSummary: הקב״ה smiled on אמציה and gave him victory over אדום. אמציה responded by bringing home their gods and bowing to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: I smiled at אמציה and gave the kings of אדום into his hand. He brought their gods and bowed to them, as the פסוק says: 'After אמציה came back from striking the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of שעיר, set them up as his gods, bowed before them, and burned incense to them.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the 'laughing' half of the פסוק. Even success did not bring the king closer to הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אמציה worshipped the gods of the very people he had beaten, which makes no sense. Together with אחז, this shows the 'fool' fails whether he is punished or rewarded, so there is 'no rest.'

keyTerms.meaning: The people of שעיר, which is אדום

phrases.english: I smiled upon Amatzyah
and I gave the kings of Edom into his hand.
He brought their gods and bowed to them,
as it is said:
"And it was after Amatzyahu came
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 25:14

phrases.english: from striking the Edomites,
that he brought the gods of the children of Seir
and set them up [for himself] as gods,
and before them he bowed,
and to them he burned incense."

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׂחַקְתִּי עִם אֲמַצְיָה וְנָתַתִּי מַלְכֵי אֱדוֹם בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'laughing' (שחק) part of the פסוק, completing the answer begun in step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When הקב״ה smiled on אמציה, אמציה still turned to idols

steps.title: רב פפא's folk saying about the master who can't tell good from bad
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says this matches a popular saying: I cried for the master and he didn't notice, I laughed for him and he didn't notice. Woe to the master who can't tell good from bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what people say: 'I cried for the master and he didn't know, I laughed for the master and he didn't know. Woe to the master who doesn't know the difference between good and bad.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא backs up the explanation with a common folk saying that makes the same point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying matches the two kings exactly. Crying stands for punishment, as with אחז. Laughing stands for kindness, as with אמציה. Someone who responds to neither one cannot be guided at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say, a folk saying

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'whether angry or laughing, there is no rest' describes the wicked kings: punishment pushed אחז to idols, and kindness pushed אמציה to idols. Neither one woke them up.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This is what people say:
I cried for the master and he did not know,
I laughed for the master and he did not know;
woe to the master
who does not know between good and bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 13 and 14 with a popular saying
steps.raayaObject: The explanation that the kings answered both anger and kindness with idol worship
steps.raayaSupportSource: A folk saying quoted by רב פפא

steps.title: The princes of Babylon sat where the סנהדרין used to rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, explains that the 'middle gate' where the princes of בבל sat was the place where הלכות were decided.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the princes of the king of בבל came and sat in the 'middle gate.' רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, says this was the place where they used to decide הלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the fall of ירושלים and explains which spot the 'middle gate' was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'middle gate' was not just any gate. It was where the סנהדרין sat and decided הלכות. So the enemy princes sat down in the holiest seat of Torah leadership, and that shows how complete the disgrace was.

keyTerms.meaning: The princes of the king of בבל

phrases.english: "And all [the princes of] the king of Babylonia came
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 39:3. The words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: (came) [and sat] in the middle gate."
phrases.notes: Some versions have 'came' (round brackets), but the corrected wording leaves it out and reads 'and sat' instead.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
It was the place in which they would decide halachos.
phrases.notes: מְחַתְּכִין ('cut' or 'decide') sounds like תָּוֶךְ. That's the hint in the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the stories about the last kings of יהודה with a new פסוק about the fall of ירושלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 'middle gate' where the princes of בבל sat was the seat where הלכות were decided.

steps.title: A popular saying: where the master hung his weapons, the lowly shepherd hangs his jug
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says this matches a popular saying: in the place where the master hangs his weapons, the lowly shepherd hangs his jug.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: this is what people say. Where the master used to hang his weapons, now the lowly shepherd hangs his jug.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא backs up רבי יוחנן's teaching with a well-known folk saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'master' stands for the סנהדרין, and the 'lowly shepherd' stands for the princes of בבל. Just as in step 15, רב פפא shows that a common saying captures the idea of the דרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what people say:
In the place where the master hangs his weapons,
there the despicable shepherd hangs his jug.
phrases.notes: The master is the סנהדרין, and the shepherd is the Babylonian princes who took over their place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַיְינוּ דְּאָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 16 with a folk saying.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's reading that the enemy sat in the seat of the סנהדרין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A popular saying about a lowly shepherd hanging his jug where the master hung his weapons

steps.title: A memory aid for the next teachings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן, a short memory aid listing key words from the teachings of רב חסדא that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: 'By the field,' '(houses) [groups],' 'shall not befall.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a short list of key words to help us remember the order of the teachings that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one teaching: 'field' is the פסוק about the lazy man's field (step 19), 'groups' is the four groups who do not greet the שכינה (step 21), and 'shall not befall' is the teaching on the פסוק 'לא תאונה אליך רעה' (step 23).

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists key words from coming teachings
Shall not befall (key words of a later teaching)

phrases.english: Mnemonic: By the field,
(houses) [groups], shall not befall.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'houses,' but the corrected wording reads 'groups,' which fits the four groups taught below.

steps.triggerLanguage: סִימַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition line. It sets up a new series of teachings from רב חסדא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A list of key words for the teachings of רב חסדא in the name of רבי ירמיה בר אבא.

steps.title: What does the פסוק about the lazy man's field mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רבי ירמיה בר אבא, asks what the פסוק in משלי about the neglected field and vineyard means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of רבי ירמיה בר אבא: what does this פסוק mean? 'I passed by the field of a lazy man, and by the vineyard of a man lacking sense. Behold, it was all overgrown with thistles, its surface was covered with nettles, and its stone wall was broken.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new דרשה by asking about a פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the surface, the פסוק describes a farm that keeps getting worse. Each stage of the ruin will be read as a different king, so the question prepares us for a step-by-step reading.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"I passed by the field of a lazy man,
and by the vineyard of a man lacking sense;
and behold, it was all overgrown with thistles,
its surface was covered with nettles,
and its stone wall was broken"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching listed in the סימן ('by the field').
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the פסוק about the ruined field and vineyard is really describing.

steps.title: Five kings who ruined the kingdom step by step
steps.stepSummary: Each part of the פסוק is one king: אחז, מנשה, אמון, יהויקים, and finally צדקיהו, in whose days the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I passed by the field of a lazy man' is אחז. 'And by the vineyard of a man lacking sense' is מנשה. 'And behold, it was all overgrown with thistles' is אמון. 'Its surface was covered with nettles' is יהויקים. 'And its stone wall was broken' is צדקיהו, in whose days the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by matching each phrase of the פסוק to a king of יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the פסוק follows the slow decline of the kingdom: neglect, then foolishness, then weeds spreading and covering everything. The last stage, the broken wall, is the final collapse under צדקיהו, when the בית המקדש was destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: King of יהודה, the 'man lacking sense'
Last king of יהודה, the 'broken wall'

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק of the neglected field is a map of the kingdom's decline. Five kings each made things worse, and it ended with the destruction of the בית המקדש in the days of צדקיהו.

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל שְׂדֵה אִישׁ עָצֵל עָבַרְתִּי״ – זֶה אָחָז,
phrases.english: "I passed by the field of a lazy man": this is Achaz.

phrases.aramaic: ״וְעַל כֶּרֶם אָדָם חֲסַר לֵב״ – זֶה מְנַשֶּׁה,
phrases.english: "And by the vineyard of a man lacking sense": this is Menashe.
"And behold, it was all overgrown with thistles": this is Amon.
"Its surface was covered with nettles": this is Yehoyakim.
"And its stone wall was broken": this is Tzidkiyahu,
in whose days the Temple was destroyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עַל שְׂדֵה אִישׁ עָצֵל עָבַרְתִּי״ – זֶה אָחָז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק describes five kings of יהודה in order: אחז, מנשה, אמון, יהויקים, צדקיהו.

steps.title: Four groups who will not greet the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רבי ירמיה בר אבא, teaches that four groups will not greet the שכינה: mockers, liars, flatterers, and people who speak לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said in the name of רבי ירמיה בר אבא: four groups do not greet the שכינה. They are the group of mockers, the group of liars, the group of flatterers, and the group of people who speak לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from the same speakers and lists four kinds of people who are kept away from the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the 'groups' item from the סימן. The list states the rule first, and the next step gives a פסוק for each group.

keyTerms.meaning: Greet (literally 'receive the face of') the שכינה

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבַּע כִּיתּוֹת אֵין מְקַבְּלוֹת פְּנֵי שְׁכִינָה:
phrases.english: Four groups do not receive the Divine Presence:
the group of mockers, the group of liars,

phrases.aramaic: כַּת חֲנֵיפִים, כַּת מְסַפְּרֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע.
phrases.english: the group of flatterers, and the group of slanderers.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same speakers, matching 'groups' in the סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mockers, liars, flatterers, and people who speak לשון הרע do not greet the שכינה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known teaching about how serious sins of speech and attitude are. They push a person away from closeness to the שכינה.

steps.title: A פסוק for each of the four groups
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each of the four groups to show that each one is kept away from the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mockers: the פסוק says, 'He withdrew His hand from mockers.' Liars: 'One who speaks lies will not stand before My eyes.' Flatterers: 'A flatterer will not come before Him.' People who speak לשון הרע: 'You are not a God Who desires wickedness; evil will not dwell with You.' This means You are righteous, and no evil will be in Your dwelling place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves each part of the list from step 21 with its own פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק shows that one kind of person is kept away from God's presence. For people who speak לשון הרע, the גמרא explains the פסוק: since God is righteous, evil cannot live in His dwelling place, so the person who speaks evil cannot be there either.

keyTerms.meaning: Will not stand before My eyes
Evil will not dwell with You

steps.whatToRemember: Four groups do not greet the שכינה: mockers, liars, flatterers, and people who speak לשון הרע. Each one has its own פסוק.

phrases.english: The group of mockers, as it is written:
"He withdrew His hand from mockers."
phrases.notes: הושע 7:5

phrases.english: The group of liars, as it is written:
"He who speaks lies shall not be established before My eyes."
phrases.notes: תהלים 101:7

phrases.english: The group of flatterers, as it is written:
"For a flatterer shall not come before Him."
phrases.notes: איוב 13:16

phrases.english: The group of slanderers, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״כִּי לֹא אֵל חָפֵץ רֶשַׁע אָתָּה לֹא יְגֻרְךָ רָע״,
phrases.english: "For You are not a God Who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 5:5

phrases.aramaic: צַדִּיק אַתָּה וְלֹא יִהְיֶה בִּמְגוּרְךָ רָע.
phrases.english: meaning: You are righteous, and there will be no evil in Your dwelling.
phrases.notes: This explains the פסוק: evil talk is 'evil,' so the person who speaks it cannot be where God dwells.

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּת לֵצִים – דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for each of the four groups listed in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that each of the four groups does not greet the שכינה
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים from הושע, תהלים, and איוב

steps.title: What does the פסוק about no evil and no plague mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting רבי ירמיה בר אבא, asks for the meaning of the פסוק in תהלים, 'No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said in the name of רבי ירמיה בר אבא: What is the meaning of the פסוק, 'No evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your tent'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב חסדא and opens it with a question about a פסוק. It is setting up the explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase מאי דכתיב signals that the plain words are not enough. 'Evil' and 'plague' sound vague, so the question is what specific troubles the פסוק promises to keep away.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said
that Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
"No evil shall befall you,
nor shall any plague come near your tent"?
phrases.notes: תהלים 91:10

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from the same chain, רב חסדא quoting רבי ירמיה בר אבא, listed in the סימן of step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What specific 'evil' and 'plague' the פסוק promises will not come.

steps.title: First explanation: no evil inclination, no doubtful נדה
steps.stepSummary: 'No evil' means the יצר הרע will not rule over them. 'No plague in your tent' means you will not come home from a trip and find your wife in a doubtful נדה state.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'No evil shall befall you' means the יצר הרע will not rule over them. 'Nor shall any plague come near your tent' means you will not find your wife in doubt whether she is a נדה when you come back from the road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining each half of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Evil' is read as the inner evil, the יצר הרע. 'Your tent' is read as your home and family life. A doubtful נדה state is pictured as a real hurt, because a husband coming home after time away is left unsure and frustrated.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether a woman has the status of נדה
From the road, back from a trip

phrases.english: "No evil shall befall you" means
that the evil inclination will not rule over them.
phrases.notes: The wording suddenly says 'them'; it means the people this blessing is talking about.

phrases.english: "Nor shall any plague come near your tent" means
that you will not find your wife
in doubt whether she is a niddah
at the time you come back from the road.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁלוֹט בָּהֶן יֵצֶר הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Evil = the יצר הרע ruling over you; plague in your tent = finding your wife in a doubtful נדה state on returning from a journey.

steps.title: Second explanation: no bad dreams, no child who sins in public
steps.stepSummary: Another reading: 'no evil' means no frightening bad dreams or thoughts. 'No plague in your tent' means you will not have a son or student who sins in public, like ישו הנוצרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: 'No evil shall befall you' means bad dreams and bad thoughts will not frighten you. 'Nor shall any plague come near your tent' means you will not have a son or student who burns his dish in public, like ישו הנוצרי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to read the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'evil' is what disturbs a person's mind, bad dreams and thoughts. 'Your tent' now means the people you raise, your children and students. 'Burning his dish in public' is a picture for sinning openly and shaming the one who raised him.

keyTerms.meaning: Burns his dish, meaning sins in public

phrases.english: Another explanation:
"No evil shall befall you" means
that bad dreams will not frighten you
nor bad thoughts.
"Nor shall any plague come near your tent" means

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא לְךָ בֵּן אוֹ תַּלְמִיד
phrases.english: that you will not have a son or a student
who burns his dish in public,
phrases.notes: A picture for someone who sins openly and brings shame on the one who raised him.

phrases.english: such as Yeshu the Notzri.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same פסוק, alongside the first answer in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Evil = frightening bad dreams and thoughts; plague in your tent = a son or student who sins publicly.

steps.title: The father's blessing ends and the mother's blessing begins
steps.stepSummary: The lines so far were the father's blessing. From here on, the next פסוקים, about angels guarding you and treading on lions and snakes, are the mother's blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until here his father blessed him; from here on his mother blessed him: 'For He will command His angels for you to guard you in all your ways. They will carry you on their hands, etc. On the lion and the snake you will tread, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא divides the מזמור into sections by speaker. It says the part we just learned was a father's blessing, and the next פסוקים are a mother's blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's part was about inner purity, a proper home, and good children and students. The mother's part is about protection: angels carrying and guarding him so nothing harms him.

phrases.english: Until here, his father blessed him;
from here on, his mother blessed him:
"For He will command His angels for you
to guard you in all your ways.
They will carry you on their hands, etc.
On the lion and the snake you will tread, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן בֵּרְכוֹ אָבִיו, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ בֵּרְכַתּוּ אִמּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Labels the פסוק explained in steps 23–25 as the father's blessing and moves on to the next פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מזמור is split by speaker: the earlier part is the father's blessing, and the פסוקים about protecting angels are the mother's blessing.

steps.title: The mother's blessing ends and Heaven's blessing begins
steps.stepSummary: The mother's blessing ends here. From this point on, the rest of the מזמור is a blessing from Heaven itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until here his mother blessed him; from here on Heaven blessed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the last section of the מזמור as Heaven's blessing. This line sets up the next פסוקים, which the גמרא will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessings climb step by step: father, then mother, then Heaven. The last section is Heaven's blessing because the מזמור there speaks as if הקב״ה Himself is talking.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא reads תהלים 91 as three layers of blessing: father (inner goodness and a good family), mother (protection by angels), and finally Heaven.

phrases.english: Until here, his mother blessed him;
from here on, Heaven blessed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן בֵּרְכַתּוּ אִמּוֹ, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ בֵּרְכַתּוּ שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the mother's section from step 26 and opens the final section, Heaven's blessing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The final section of the מזמור is a blessing from Heaven.
